Layer

Algorithms

Finalize and follow the process in dev/set-up.md.
Keep this file updated at every status change.
Define accountability link examples for high-risk claims.
Add a small script/CI job for the required automation QA checklist.





Host the documentation from bgms-docs while keeping the public URL at https://bayesian-graphical-modelling-lab.github.io/bgms/.
Add GitHub Actions workflow in bgms-docs to render Quarto and deploy to the publishing target used by the bgms website.
Configure deployment credentials (fine-grained PAT or GitHub App) with least-privilege access.
Document deployment and rollback steps for maintainers.





Define a process to monitor upstream bgms repository changes for documentation impact.
Add criteria for when code/API changes require documentation updates.
Add attribution/licensing note after confirming terms for reused Quarto website structure/content.
Investigate similar projects for attribution, content licensing, and trademark notices.
Optional future check: if Positron website assets/templates are introduced later, reassess attribution and license compatibility.
Deferred: draft docs/attribution.md template and README.md provenance boilerplate after licensing position is confirmed.




Event-driven alerts:

In bgms repo: add workflow that detects docs-impacting file changes and sends repository_dispatch to bgms-docs.
In bgms repo: define docs-impacting path filters (R/**, src/**, man/**, NAMESPACE, DESCRIPTION, NEWS*, selected vignettes/**).
In bgms-docs repo: add workflow triggered by repository_dispatch to create or update a docs-sync issue immediately.
In bgms-docs repo: issue body should include commit SHA, PR number/title, changed files summary, compare URL, and trigger timestamp.

Scheduled checks:

Add weekly scheduled workflow in bgms-docs to compare latest processed bgms SHA with upstream default branch SHA.
Add monthly scheduled workflow option (configurable) for lower-noise periods.
Ensure scheduled run opens/updates issue only when there is meaningful delta.

Triage workflow:

Auto-apply labels on created/updated issue: docs-sync, needs-triage.
Add triage decision checklist to issue template: no-doc-change, minor-doc-update, major-doc-update.
Auto-convert triage decision to follow-up issue labels (minor, major, blocked) when triage is completed.
Keep one rolling tracking issue per release cycle to avoid issue spam.

Reliability and security:

Configure cross-repo auth using least-privilege token (BGMS_DOCS_DISPATCH_TOKEN) stored as repository secret.
Add idempotency guard so the same commit/PR event is not appended twice.
Add failure notification path (workflow summary + optional issue comment) when dispatch or API update fails.

Optional enhancements:

In bgms PR template: add checkbox “This change may require docs updates” and map to docs-impact label.
If docs-impact label is set, force dispatch regardless of path-filter outcome.
Add contributor docs in README.md describing how automated docs-sync signals are generated and triaged.




Layout-impact guardrails:

Capture visual baseline for home, one guide page, one reference page, one manual page, in both light and dark mode.
Define acceptance criteria per page type (navbar, sidebar, TOC, heading scale, code readability, mobile nav).
Use change sequencing: replace styles/scripts first, then remove legacy files after replacement behavior is verified.
For each de-risking PR, include before/after screenshots and a short note on intentional layout changes.
Keep a rollback path: avoid deleting original files until replacement CSS/JS has passed review.

Keep:

Keep Quarto-generated runtime assets in docs/site_libs/ as standard framework output; do not hand-edit generated files.
Keep overall information architecture pattern (navbar + sidebar + TOC) as implementation pattern, not copied branding.
Keep package-specific content structure in guide/, reference/, and manual/.

Change:

Refactor index.css hero/banner layout to diverge clearly from inherited skeleton.
Rewrite theme.scss token choices to a bgms-specific design system.
Rewrite theme-dark.scss custom rules and remove Quarto/Posit-specific language.
Review and simplify js.html behavior; keep only behavior needed for bgms docs UX.
Update styles.css to remove “Quarto-inspired” framing and define explicit bgms branding tokens.

Remove or archive:

Remove _quarto.yml.quarto-web-original when internal reference is no longer needed.
Remove or replace filters/tools-tabset.lua if tools-tabset UI is unused; otherwise rewrite labels/icons/text.
Remove leftover Quarto/Posit naming in comments, alt text, class names, and metadata when not functionally required.

Governance and traceability:

Add docs/attribution.md with explicit acknowledgments and links once licensing/permission is clarified.
Add provenance note in README.md describing what was adapted vs rewritten.
Record source map in docs/attribution.md: adapted elements vs original bgms work.
Add release checklist item: design de-risking pass completed before first public deployment.

Basic Example

library(bgms)

Teaches concepts and walks through analyses. A reader who finishes the Guide can fit models, interpret output, and set priors with confidence.

Purpose

What is a graphical model? Nodes, edges, conditional independence.

Why Bayesian? Posterior, prior, credible intervals, Bayes factors.

Gaussian graphical model: continuous data, partial correlations, precision matrix.


guide/omrf.qmd
Ordinal MRF: ordinal/binary data, category thresholds, Blume-Capel parameterization.


guide/mixed-model.qmd
Mixed MRF: datasets with both continuous and discrete variables.


Analyses

Bayesian edge selection: inclusion Bayes factors, posterior inclusion probabilities. Includes analysis-specific prior guidance.


guide/group-comparison.qmd
Comparing networks across groups with bgmCompare(). Includes analysis-specific prior guidance.


guide/clustering.qmd
Stochastic block model for edge clustering. Includes analysis-specific prior guidance.


MCMC output

What the sampler returns: posterior samples, summary statistics, raw output structure.


guide/mcmc-diagnostics.qmd
Convergence checks: ESS, R-hat, trace plots, divergences, E-BFMI.



Pedagogical flow: Background → Models → Analyses → MCMC output. Each analysis page includes a short prior section specific to that analysis, so readers learn about priors in context rather than in the abstract.



One page per exported function or function family. Content is extracted from roxygen documentation with minimal paraphrasing.







Page
Purpose




reference/index.qmd
Section landing page with function index.


reference/bgm.qmd
bgm(): all arguments, defaults, return structure.


reference/bgmCompare.qmd
bgmCompare(): all arguments, defaults, return structure.


reference/methods.qmd
S3 methods: print, plot, summary, simulate, predict.


reference/extractors.qmd
Extractor functions: extract_arguments, extract_indicators, extract_posterior_inclusion_probabilities, extract_sbm.


reference/datasets.qmd
Bundled datasets.






For developers and methodologists who need to understand how bgms works under the hood. Each page explains a subsystem with reference to the actual code.







Page
Purpose




manual/index.qmd
Section landing page and subsystem map.


Architecture



manual/architecture.qmd
Top-level design: R front-end → C++ engine. The three-stage pipeline (bgm_spec → run_sampler → build_output). Package directory layout.


manual/r-scaffolding.qmd
The R layer in detail: validation pipeline (validate_data, validate_variable_types, validate_sampler), spec construction (bgm_spec, new_bgm_spec, validate_bgm_spec), sampler dispatch (run_sampler → model-specific C++ entry points), output assembly (build_output → posterior summaries, raw samples, diagnostics). Data flow diagram from user call to returned fit object.


manual/model-classes.qmd
C++ class hierarchy: BaseModel → GGMModel, OMRFModel, MixedMRFModel. Virtual interface (capability queries, parameter access, edge selection, adaptation, missing data). How models register their storage layout.


MCMC engine



manual/samplers.qmd
Sampler hierarchy: SamplerBase → MetropolisSampler, GradientSamplerBase → HMCSampler, NUTSSampler, HybridNUTSSampler. Step-size adaptation, mass matrix tuning. Factory dispatch by sampler_type string.


manual/nuts.qmd
NUTS algorithm: recursive tree-building, U-turn criterion, multinomial sampling, divergence detection. How tree depth and energy diagnostics are recorded.


manual/warmup.qmd
Three-stage adaptive warmup schedule: stage 1 (step-size), stage 2 (mass matrix), stage 3a (final step-size). Edge-selection phases 3b (proposal-SD tuning) and 3c (graph initialization). How WarmupSchedule coordinates sampler and model.


manual/parallel-chains.qmd
Parallel chain execution: model.clone() / edge_prior.clone() per chain, TBB thread control via tbb::global_control, RcppParallel::parallelFor dispatch through MCMCChainRunner. Sequential fallback for single-thread mode. Per-chain RNG seeding (config.seed + chain_id). Progress tracking and user-interrupt handling across threads.


Models



manual/ggm-internals.qmd
GGM implementation: precision matrix parameterization, Cholesky updates (cholupdate), continuous-data likelihood and gradient, edge-specific Metropolis proposals.


manual/omrf-internals.qmd
OMRF implementation: ordinal threshold parameterization, Blume-Capel model with linear + quadratic effects, pseudo-likelihood, full-conditional Gibbs steps for edge indicators.


manual/variable-helpers.qmd
Numerically stable computation for MRF variables. The FAST/SAFE dual-path strategy: precomputed exponentials and power-chain accumulation when exponents are bounded (FAST path), direct log-sum-exp evaluation as fallback (SAFE path). Covers compute_denom_ordinal, compute_denom_blume_capel, compute_probs_ordinal, compute_probs_blume_capel, joint LogZAndProbs computation. The EXP_BOUND = 709 threshold and contiguous-block scanning for branch-free vectorization.


manual/mixed-internals.qmd
Mixed MRF implementation: block structure (discrete-discrete, continuous-continuous, cross-type), how the sampler handles mixed parameter vectors.


Priors and edge selection



manual/edge-priors.qmd
Edge prior framework: BaseEdgePrior interface, Beta-Bernoulli default, unit-information prior. How inclusion probabilities and Bayes factors are computed.


manual/sbm-prior.qmd
Stochastic block model prior: MFM-SBM formulation, Gibbs block-allocation updates, how cluster structure regularizes edge inclusion. The StochasticBlockEdgePrior class.


Group comparison



manual/bgmcompare-internals.qmd
bgmCompare engine: separate sampler, multi-group log-posterior and gradient, output handling. How it differs from single-group bgm.


Numerical methods



manual/numerical.qmd
Numerical stability toolkit: custom exp/log macros (explog_macros.h), Cholesky rank-1 updates, the FAST/SAFE pattern. Cross-references variable-helpers.qmd for the full dual-path story.






Complete, self-contained analyses from data to interpretation. Each example uses a bundled or simulated dataset and runs end-to-end.







Page
Purpose

Section landing page.

Binary data → OMRF → edge selection → interpretation.


examples/ordinal-network.qmd
Ordinal data → OMRF → edge selection → interpretation.

Continuous data → GGM → edge selection → interpretation.

Mixed data → Mixed MRF → edge selection → interpretation.


examples/group-comparison.qmd
Two-group data → bgmCompare() → network differences.


examples/clustering.qmd
Edge clustering via SBM prior → block structure.

Title.
3–6 section headings.

Render the site. Fix broken links, missing nav entries, and heading hierarchy issues.

All target .qmd files exist.
No broken links.
Heading depth ≤ 3.
Navigation entries are present.

Recommended order: Build all skeletons before populating any page.




Goal: Fill pages with facts from sources. Mark where each fact came from.
Do this for reference pages:

Pull function signatures, arguments, return values, and examples from roxygen/man.
Use deterministic extraction tooling where possible (.Rd parsing, tools::Rd2txt()).
Insert with minimal paraphrasing first.

Do this for guide and manual pages:

Pull from algorithm design notes and implementation comments.
Convert into plain-language explanations.

For all pages:

Add provenance markers to important claims so you can trace where text came from:

SOURCE: R/<file>.R#<function>
SOURCE: man/<topic>.Rd
SOURCE: design/<note>.md#<section>

For high-risk claims (defaults, priors, convergence, sampling, core API), add accountability links that point a reader or developer straight to the source. This is a hard release gate for high-risk claims. Best effort for low-risk narrative text.

Done when: Each major claim has a provenance marker.
Recommended order:

Guide pages next (user task flow).

Goal: Improve clarity without changing facts.
Do this:

Ask LLMs to rewrite for readability only.
Enforce these constraints:

Do not add undocumented features.

model classes

Flag jargon, unclear steps, or confusing structure.
Log review decisions.

Commit fixes: docs(review): <description of fix>.
Update status to Reviewed in dev/task-list.md.

Done when: Each high-risk page has both sign-offs recorded in the task board.




Work in short cycles: 2–3 days, 3–6 pages per cycle.
At the end of each cycle, produce:

A rendered preview.
An open issues list.
An accepted pages list.







Goal: Make the whole site feel like one voice.
Do this:

Standardize terminology across sections.
Normalize heading patterns and cross-links.
Enforce STYLE_GUIDE.md conventions.
Ensure examples match current API signatures.

Done when: No style inconsistencies across sections.




Goal: Final automated and human checks, then deploy.



Full render succeeds.
No broken links.
Search index sanity check passes.
No unresolved TODO: markers.
No malformed SOURCE: markers.
All runnable R code executes without error on every page.





Desktop and mobile visual sanity.
Navigation and table-of-contents behavior.
Zero unresolved factual issues.





Final sign-off by both Maarten and Emily.
Update status to Approved in dev/task-list.md.
Merge cycle branch into main and deploy.

Done when: Site is live and all pages show Approved.





A page can only be marked Approved if all of these are true:

Structure matches section template.
Facts verified against source hierarchy.
No unresolved TODOs.
Cross-links resolve.
Terminology consistent with related pages.
Reviewer notes resolved.
Automated QA checks pass.

After the first release, keep docs aligned with the package:

If you want visibility into progress, track per cycle:

Purpose




manual/index.qmd
Section landing page and subsystem map.


Architecture



manual/architecture.qmd
Top-level design: R front-end → C++ engine. The three-stage pipeline (bgm_spec → run_sampler → build_output). Package directory layout.


manual/r-scaffolding.qmd
The R layer in detail: validation pipeline (validate_data, validate_variable_types, validate_sampler), spec construction (bgm_spec, new_bgm_spec, validate_bgm_spec), sampler dispatch (run_sampler → model-specific C++ entry points), output assembly (build_output → posterior summaries, raw samples, diagnostics). Data flow diagram from user call to returned fit object.


manual/model-classes.qmd
C++ class hierarchy: BaseModel → GGMModel, OMRFModel, MixedMRFModel. Virtual interface (capability queries, parameter access, edge selection, adaptation, missing data). How models register their storage layout.


MCMC engine



manual/samplers.qmd
Sampler hierarchy: SamplerBase → MetropolisSampler, GradientSamplerBase → HMCSampler, NUTSSampler, HybridNUTSSampler. Step-size adaptation, mass matrix tuning. Factory dispatch by sampler_type string.


manual/nuts.qmd
NUTS algorithm: recursive tree-building, U-turn criterion, multinomial sampling, divergence detection. How tree depth and energy diagnostics are recorded.


manual/warmup.qmd
Three-stage adaptive warmup schedule: stage 1 (step-size), stage 2 (mass matrix), stage 3a (final step-size). Edge-selection phases 3b (proposal-SD tuning) and 3c (graph initialization). How WarmupSchedule coordinates sampler and model.


manual/parallel-chains.qmd
Parallel chain execution: model.clone() / edge_prior.clone() per chain, TBB thread control via tbb::global_control, RcppParallel::parallelFor dispatch through MCMCChainRunner. Sequential fallback for single-thread mode. Per-chain RNG seeding (config.seed + chain_id). Progress tracking and user-interrupt handling across threads.


Models



manual/ggm-internals.qmd
GGM implementation: precision matrix parameterization, Cholesky updates (cholupdate), continuous-data likelihood and gradient, edge-specific Metropolis proposals.


manual/omrf-internals.qmd
OMRF implementation: ordinal threshold parameterization, Blume-Capel model with linear + quadratic effects, pseudo-likelihood, full-conditional Gibbs steps for edge indicators.


manual/variable-helpers.qmd
Numerically stable computation for MRF variables. The FAST/SAFE dual-path strategy: precomputed exponentials and power-chain accumulation when exponents are bounded (FAST path), direct log-sum-exp evaluation as fallback (SAFE path). Covers compute_denom_ordinal, compute_denom_blume_capel, compute_probs_ordinal, compute_probs_blume_capel, joint LogZAndProbs computation. The EXP_BOUND = 709 threshold and contiguous-block scanning for branch-free vectorization.


manual/mixed-internals.qmd
Mixed MRF implementation: block structure (discrete-discrete, continuous-continuous, cross-type), how the sampler handles mixed parameter vectors.


Priors and edge selection



manual/edge-priors.qmd
Edge prior framework: BaseEdgePrior interface, Beta-Bernoulli default, unit-information prior. How inclusion probabilities and Bayes factors are computed.


manual/sbm-prior.qmd
Stochastic block model prior: MFM-SBM formulation, Gibbs block-allocation updates, how cluster structure regularizes edge inclusion. The StochasticBlockEdgePrior class.


Group comparison



manual/bgmcompare-internals.qmd
bgmCompare engine: separate sampler, multi-group log-posterior and gradient, output handling. How it differs from single-group bgm.


Numerical methods



manual/numerical.qmd
Numerical stability toolkit: custom exp/log macros (explog_macros.h), Cholesky rank-1 updates, the FAST/SAFE pattern. Cross-references variable-helpers.qmd for the full dual-path story.






Complete, self-contained analyses from data to interpretation. Each example uses a bundled or simulated dataset and runs end-to-end.

Purpose

title: bgm
text: Bayesian estimation of graphical models for binary and/or ordinal variables.

title: bgm
text:
Description
bgm() fits a Bayesian graphical model using MCMC sampling. The model can handle ordinal variables (ordinal MRF) or continuous variables (Gaussian graphical model).

title: bgm
text:
Usage
bgm(
 x,
 variable_type = "ordinal",
 reference_category,
 iter = 10000,
 burnin = 1000,
 ...
)

title: bgm
text:
Arguments







Argument
Description




x
A data frame or matrix of observations.


variable_type
Character; "ordinal" (default) or "continuous".


reference_category
Reference category for ordinal variables.


iter
Number of MCMC iterations after burnin.


burnin
Number of burnin iterations.


...
Additional arguments (see documentation).

title: bgm
text:
Value
An object of class bgms containing:

interactions — Posterior samples for edge weights
thresholds — Posterior samples for threshold parameters

gamma — Edge inclusion indicators
prior — Prior specification used

title: bgm
text:
Examples

library(bgms)
data(Wenchuan)

# Basic usage
fit <- bgm(Wenchuan)
summary(fit)

# With edge selection
fit <- bgm(Wenchuan, edge_selection = TRUE)

title: bgmCompare
text: Compare graphical models between groups.

title: bgmCompare
text:
Description
bgmCompare() tests for differences in network structure between independent groups using Bayes factor tests.

title: bgmCompare
text:
Usage
bgmCompare(
  x,
  group,
  ...
)

title: bgmCompare
text:
Arguments



Argument
Description




x
A data frame or matrix of observations.


group
A factor or vector indicating group membership.


...
Additional arguments passed to the sampler.

title: bgmCompare
text:
Value
An object of class bgmCompare containing posterior samples and Bayes factors for group differences.

title: bgmCompare
text:
Examples

library(bgms)

# Simulated example
# fit <- bgmCompare(data, group = group_variable)
# summary(fit)

title: bgmCompare
text:
See Also
bgm(), summary.bgmCompare
